newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Fresh violence hits French Guianan capital.
newsitem.headline: Fresh violence hits French Guianan capital.

text.p: Violence erupted in the French Guianan capital Cayenne for the fourth night in a week on Thursday as youths looted stores and clashed with police, witnesses said.

Armed youths erected a barricade on a major boulevard outside the city centre halting traffic. Police fired teargas to disperse the crowd which had robbed stores, set fire to plastic garbage bins and burned tyres.
Local state-owned radio said rioters had fired shotguns at paramilitary policeman and one officer was wounded in the spine. They said police arrested 13 and seven remained in custody.
Two firearms stores have been looted in well organised attacks, the store owners and French officials said.
The French territory, which lies on the southwest coast between Brazil and Surinam, is the only non-independent state in South America.
On Wednesday France's administrator (prefect) in Guiana Piere Dartout said the violence was a "well organised, deliberate effort to destabilise French Guiana."
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahatir Mohamed told a news conference he was sure the French would be able to deal with the situation.

Mahatir Mohamed was in French Guiana for the launch of a Malaysian satellite aboard an Ariane rocket from the European Space Agency launch centre at Kourou. The launch went off without incident and no violence was reported in the space city.
Paris flew 200 paramilitary riot police reinforcements to the territory over the weekend after local police were overwhelmed by the rioting.

French Guiana's international airport near Cayenne was shut on Wednesday at the request of an inter-union group protesting against government policy in French Guiana and the arrest of rioters following the first wave of violence late last week.
High school students protesting against poor conditions in local schools sparked the riots when their strike degenerated into clashes between police and youths.
The French government has promised to hold wide-ranging talks on the situation next year.
French Guiana's economy lags behind that of mainland France and it has an unemployment rate approaching 25 percent of the labour force. Unemployment is particularly acute among the young.
